statements.quote: This is great news for the Paducah community, and I want to thank President Trump for selecting the Paducah Site to host new AI infrastructure.
statements.context: McConnell praised the Department of Energy's choice of the Paducah, Kentucky site as one of four federal locations for AI data centers and energy projects.
statements.reason: Promotes AI infrastructure in Kentucky and does not mention any risk from AI.

statements.venue: Remarks at the CSIS Global Security Forum on defense innovation
statements.quote: But advanced, autonomous systems have not supplanted the traditional ways of war.
statements.context: McConnell argued that new military technology, including autonomous systems and artificial intelligence, does not replace the need for conventional weapons and larger defense budgets.
statements.reason: About military use of autonomous systems and AI, with no catastrophic risk from AI named (ruling 3).

pause.note: No statement found on pausing AI development. His 1 July 2025 vote concerned a ban on state AI laws, not a pause on AI development, so it does not count here.

record: Praised the selection of the Department of Energy's Paducah Site for AI data center and energy infrastructure, and said he had earlier contacted Energy Secretary Chris Wright in support of Paducah's bid.
Voted Yea on the Blackburn amendment (No. 2814) that removed the proposed ban on state AI regulation from the budget reconciliation bill; the amendment passed 99 to 1.

Announced $41 million in federal funding for a program support facility at the Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant, which his office said would also support artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies expected at the site.
grade_reason: The only AI remarks found since January 2025 promote AI infrastructure in Kentucky and mention AI in passing in a defense speech. Nothing found acknowledges catastrophic risk from AI.
notes: All six required web searches ran on 11 November 2026 (official site, superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, pause or moratorium, China agreement, 'AI safety'); none returned a statement by McConnell on AI risk, superintelligence, a pause, or an AI agreement with China. News articles from September 2026 on Congress and AI extinction warnings, and on Republicans resisting or splitting over AI safety laws, were opened where possible (local12.com: no mention of him; newschannel9.com: only photo captions were readable, no mention). An earlier run also opened mcconnell.senate.gov press release listing pages 1 to 6 (6 February 2025 to 26 October 2026; January 2025 not checked) and reviewed titles only, plus the 12 May 2026 defense budget hearing remarks and the 23 September 2026 Taiwan letter release, neither of which mentioned AI. Pages were read through a fetch tool that answers questions about a page rather than returning its full text; in this run I asked it to confirm both quotes against the pages and it reported both present word for word, with the 2025-07-24 quote now extended to the full sentence. A reviewer should still confirm both character for character. The 15 January 2026 and 17 February 2026 funding releases mention artificial intelligence only in the office's description of a Paducah facility, not in his own words, so they are in `record` and not in `statements`. The 1 July 2025 vote is recorded as a fact only; no statement by him explaining it was found. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (Sanders and Casar, September 2026): no source names him as a co-sponsor; the Sanders summary sheet and the news reports opened name only Sanders and Casar, but the official co-sponsor list on congress.gov was not checked. One search result (mezha.net, on Senate AI safety bill talks) could not be opened (HTTP 403); the search summary said it mentioned him only in connection with his return to the Capitol after a fall. An Axios newsletter of 14 September 2026 could not be opened in the earlier run (HTTP 403). Out of date range and so left out: his May 2024 opposition at a Rules Committee markup to bills on AI deepfakes in political ads. He was hospitalized and absent for about three months in mid-2026, which may partly explain the thin record.
